<objective>
Seal the handover: give a member holding a temporary password somewhere to choose their own,
show a signed-in member who they are with one click to leave, and retire the shared kiosk
passcode at the shed router.

Purpose: the server has refused every other page to a flagged member since plan 01-02, and the
route guard has pointed at /set-password since plan 01-05. This plan builds the screen both of
them point at, adds the top bar slot a self-owned sign-in needs, and makes the first success
criterion of the phase true.

Output: /set-password, the top bar name and sign-out slot, and the router change.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    Tests in `src/web/lib/password-check.test.ts`:
    - `checkNewPassword` accepts twelve characters and rejects eleven.
    - It rejects 129 characters and accepts 128.
    - It reports a mismatch when the two entries differ.
    - When both rules fail it reports the length failure only.
    - It reports nothing for a valid, matching pair.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Create `src/web/lib/password-check.ts` as a plain module: `MIN_LENGTH` of 12 and `MAX_LENGTH` of 128, mirroring the server, and `checkNewPassword(next, again)` returning a tagged result.

Create `src/web/pages/set-password.tsx` to match the sign-in screen: same centred card, same fixed message strip above the fields.

Checks run on Save only. The length rule is printed before typing starts, so no message ever has to appear mid-keystroke.

Both fields stop at 128 characters, and the server enforces the limit again on its own.

The screen's bare header carries a sign-out control, so a member who cannot recall the temporary password a steward gave them is not stuck.

On success go straight to `/sheds`; on failure show the server's message in the same strip. Every visible string comes from `SET_PASSWORD_COPY`.
  </action>
  <verify>

  </verify>

<task type="checkpoint:human-action" gate="blocking">
  <name>Task 3: Router change — drop the shared passcode prompt</name>
  <reversibility rating="costly">Putting the prompt back means redoing the router rule from scratch and would again lock out stewards who rely on the old passcode.</reversibility>
  <read_first>
    - .planning/STATE.md § Blockers (the passcode item this removal closes)
    - .planning/phases/01-member-sign-in-sessions/01-CONTEXT.md § D-07
    - docs/kiosk-retirement.md (the notes this task extends)
  </read_first>
  <action>
    Remove the passcode rule for the lendshed.example host from the shed router's admin page,
    then confirm the app signs members in entirely on its own.

    This is a manual step: the rule lives in the router's own settings, and nothing in this
    repository or this environment can reach them.
  </action>
  <instructions>
    Before removing anything:
    1. Confirm at least one member account exists and can sign in. Run `lendctl list` on the
       shed box, and if it is empty run `lendctl create` for the first steward.
    2. Confirm the deployed server is the new build: a request with no session cookie must get 401.

    Then, on the router admin page:
    3. Delete the passcode rule for the host. The tunnel to the shed box stays.

    Then verify, in this order:
    4. In a fresh browser profile, load the host. The app's own sign-in form must be the only prompt.
    5. Sign in with the account from step 1, set a new password when asked, and confirm you land on /sheds with your name and sign-out visible.
    6. Confirm the live-status dot turns green and an export download starts, then sign out and confirm both are refused.
    7. Confirm the certificate check path on the host answers with no prompt in front of it.
  </instructions>
  <verification>
    - Step 4: a fresh browser profile sees the app's own sign-in form as the only prompt.
    - Step 5: signing in lands on the password screen, and saving lands on /sheds with the name and sign-out shown.
    - Step 6: the status socket and a download both work while signed in and both refuse after sign-out.
    - Step 7: the certificate check path answers without a prompt.
  </verification>
  <resume-signal>Report steps 4 through 7 one by one, then type "router done" or describe what failed</resume-signal>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser → server `POST /api/set-password` | A restricted session submits new password text here. |
| route guard → browser (`lendshed_name` cookie) | A script-readable cookie that carries a display name. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01-34 | Elevation of Privilege | the whole app once the router prompt is gone | critical | mitigate | The checklist needs a working account and a verified new build before the rule is deleted. |
| T-01-35 | Information Disclosure | the `lendshed_name` cookie | low | accept | It holds a name the member already sees on screen and never a token. |
| T-01-36 | Spoofing | a forged `lendshed_name` cookie | low | accept | Display only; every decision reads the HttpOnly session cookie on the server. |
| T-01-37 | Elevation of Privilege | the forced screen skipped by editing the URL | high | mitigate | The guard and the server each refuse other routes for a flagged session. |
| T-01-SC | Tampering | package installs | low | mitigate | This plan adds no dependency. |
</threat_model>

<flagged_assumptions>
- The `lendshed_name` cookie is a planner choice: the design wants the name with no fetch, and reading
  request headers in the root layout would make every route dynamic. A guard-written cookie avoids that.
- Steps 4 through 7 of the router change cannot be automated from this repository and are recorded
  in `01-VALIDATION.md` as manual-only checks.
</flagged_assumptions>
